questions.stem: BHARAT RATNA, India's HIGHEST CIVILIAN AWARD, was instituted in:
questions.explanation: BHARAT RATNA — India's HIGHEST CIVILIAN AWARD. INSTITUTED on 2 JANUARY 1954 by President Rajendra Prasad. Originally awarded for 'exceptional service of the highest order in any field of human endeavour' — arts, literature, sciences, public services. EXPANDED 2011 (Rule amendment) to explicitly include SPORTS + any field of human endeavour. DESIGN: PIPAL LEAF (SACRED FIG, Bodhi tree-leaf) shape; BRONZE; inscription 'BHARAT RATNA' in Hindi + 'SUN' in the centre, + embossed platinum sun; 'SATYAMEV JAYATE' in Hindi on reverse. Worn around neck on WHITE ribbon. NOT a formal 'title' (Art 18 of Constitution prohibits titles) — recipients cannot use it as prefix/suffix to their name (though commonly referred to as 'Bharat Ratna X'). ELIGIBILITY: PM recommends to PRESIDENT. NO formal recommendation needed (unlike Padma). MAX 3 PER YEAR conventionally (not a strict rule); years with no award are common. POSTHUMOUS allowed SINCE 1955 (Lal Bahadur Shastri first posthumous). INCLUDES cash benefit? NO — only certificate + medallion. Railway passes + VIP protocol benefits. RECIPIENTS till 2024: 53 individuals. FIRST 3 (1954): (1) Dr. SARVEPALLI RADHAKRISHNAN — philosopher + 2nd President. (2) C. RAJAGOPALACHARI — 'Rajaji', first Indian Governor-General, freedom fighter, statesman. (3) Dr. CHANDRASEKHARA VENKATA RAMAN — Nobel laureate Physicist (Raman Effect). NOTABLE RECIPIENTS (select): (4) DR BHAGWAN DAS (1955). (5) MOKSHAGUNDAM VISVESVARAYA (1955, engineer). (6) PANDIT GOVIND BALLABH PANT (1957). (7) PANDIT JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (1955, while PM — self-recommendation controversial). (8) DR RAJENDRA PRASAD (1962, as President). (9) MOTHER TERESA (1980, Nobel Peace laureate). (10) INDIRA GANDHI (1971, as PM). (11) M.G. RAMACHANDRAN (1988, TN CM + actor). (12) Dr. B.R. AMBEDKAR (1990 posthumous). (13) NELSON MANDELA (1990 — 2nd non-Indian after Abdul Ghaffar Khan 1987). (14) RAJIV GANDHI (1991 posthumous). (15) Sardar VALLABHBHAI PATEL (1991 posthumous). (16) Maulana ABUL KALAM AZAD (1992 posthumous). (17) J.R.D. TATA (1992). (18) SATYAJIT RAY (1992, filmmaker). (19) A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM (1997 — before becoming President). (20) AMARTYA SEN (1999, Nobel Economics). (21) RAVI SHANKAR (1999, sitar maestro). (22) LATA MANGESHKAR (2001, 'Nightingale of India'). (23) BHIMSEN JOSHI (2008, Hindustani vocalist). (24) Prof. C.N.R. RAO (2014, chemist). (25) SACHIN TENDULKAR (2014 — FIRST sportsperson + youngest at 40). (26) ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE (2015). (27) MADAN MOHAN MALAVIYA (2015 posthumous). (28) PRANAB MUKHERJEE (2019, ex-President). (29) NANAJI DESHMUKH (2019 posthumous). (30) Dr BHUPEN HAZARIKA (2019 posthumous). (31) P.V. NARASIMHA RAO (2024 posthumous). (32) CHAUDHARY CHARAN SINGH (2024 posthumous). (33) M.S. SWAMINATHAN (2024 posthumous, Green Revolution father). (34) L.K. ADVANI (2024, BJP veteran, still living — among rare). (35) KARPOORI THAKUR (2024 posthumous, Bihar socialist CM). LATEST year had RECORD 5 awards (unusual). NON-INDIAN recipients: KHAN ABDUL GHAFFAR KHAN 'Frontier Gandhi' (Pakistan, 1987) + NELSON MANDELA (1990). MOTHER TERESA was Indian citizen since 1951 + thus considered Indian recipient. by President Rajendra Prasad; originally for arts/lit/science/public service; expanded 2011 to include sports + any human endeavour.

questions.stem: The FIRST Bharat Ratna recipient was:

options.option_text: Dr SARVEPALLI RADHAKRISHNAN (1954) — philosopher-statesman; 2nd President of India (1962-67); Teachers' Day 5 Sep = his birthday

questions.explanation: Dr. SARVEPALLI RADHAKRISHNAN (5 Sep 1888 – 17 Apr 1975) — first recipient of Bharat Ratna (1954, along with CV Raman + Rajagopalachari). Indian philosopher, statesman, second PRESIDENT of India. BIRTH: Tiruttani, Madras Presidency (now TN); died Madras 1975. EDUCATION: Christian College Madras (MA Philosophy 1906-09 — influenced by missionary critique of Hinduism, responded to it). TEACHING: Assistant professor Madras Presidency College 1909; moved to Mysore University + Calcutta University; Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions + Ethics at Oxford (1936-52) — first Indian in that chair. VICE CHANCELLOR of Andhra University (1931-36) + BHU (1939-48) + Chairman of University Education Commission (1948-49). Won great RESPECT in academic world. PHILOSOPHICAL WORKS: (1) 'THE PHILOSOPHY OF RABINDRANATH TAGORE' (1918). (2) 'THE REIGN OF RELIGION IN CONTEMPORARY PHILOSOPHY' (1920). (3) 'INDIAN PHILOSOPHY' (2 vols 1923-27). (4) 'THE HINDU VIEW OF LIFE' (1927 — Oxford Upton lectures). (5) 'AN IDEALIST VIEW OF LIFE' (1932 — Hibbert Lectures). (6) 'EASTERN RELIGIONS + WESTERN THOUGHT' (1939). (7) Translations: Bhagavad Gita (1948), Upanishads, Dhammapada, Brahmasutras. Championed modernised Advaita Vedanta. KEY IDEAS: Hinduism is tolerant + universal; Self-realization through intuition; religion + science complementary; emphasis on 'religious experience' over dogma; India as 'living laboratory' of religions. TRIBUTE by BERTRAND RUSSELL: 'It is an honour for philosophy that Radhakrishnan should have been Vice-President of India'. POLITICAL CAREER: (1) AMBASSADOR to USSR (1949-52) — Nehru's appointment despite not being politician; developed rapport with Stalin; praised Soviet anti-caste policies. (2) VICE-PRESIDENT of India (1952-62) + Chairman of Rajya Sabha. (3) PRESIDENT of INDIA (13 May 1962 – 13 May 1967) — SUCCEEDED Dr Rajendra Prasad. Second President. Oversaw 1962 Sino-Indian War + 1965 Indo-Pak War. Delivered celebrated Republic Day addresses. HONOURS: (1) BHARAT RATNA 1954 (first batch). (2) KNIGHTHOOD from British 1931 (never formally used title). (3) 27+ honorary doctorates. (4) Order of Merit (UK) 1963. TEACHERS' DAY on 5 September = his birthday — declared in 1962 when students asked to celebrate his birthday + he replied 'Instead of celebrating my birthday, it would be my proud privilege if September 5 is observed as Teachers' Day'. DIED 17 April 1975 in Madras. RADHAKRISHNAN legacy: ideal scholar-statesman; bridged Indian + Western thought; presented Hinduism to the West as a rational religion. FAMOUS quote: 'Teachers should be the best minds of the country'. Wrote philosophically + with grace; his 1929 Hibbert Lecture 'An Idealist View of Life' is considered a classic.

questions.stem: The HIERARCHY of Indian CIVILIAN AWARDS (highest to lowest) is:

options.option_text: Padma Shri → Padma Bhushan → Padma Vibhushan → Bharat Ratna
BHARAT RATNA → PADMA VIBHUSHAN → PADMA BHUSHAN → PADMA SHRI
Arjuna Award → Dronacharya → Khel Ratna → Bharat Ratna
Param Vir Chakra → Ashok Chakra → Vir Chakra

questions.explanation: INDIA's CIVILIAN AWARD HIERARCHY (highest to lowest, per Order of Precedence): (1) BHARAT RATNA (1954) — HIGHEST. 'Ornate pipal leaf'. 'Exceptional service of highest order'. (2) PADMA VIBHUSHAN (1954) — 2nd highest. 'Exceptional + distinguished service' in any field. 'Lotus' design. (3) PADMA BHUSHAN (1954) — 3rd highest. 'Distinguished service of a high order'. (4) PADMA SHRI (1954) — 4th highest. 'Distinguished service' in any field. COLLECTIVELY, the three Padma awards = 'PADMA AWARDS'. All instituted 2 Jan 1954 (along with Bharat Ratna, by President Rajendra Prasad). AWARD PROCESS: (1) Any CITIZEN can NOMINATE any deserving person via online PadmaAwards.gov.in portal or Rashtrapati Bhavan. (2) Nominations scrutinised by PADMA AWARDS COMMITTEE (constituted annually under Home Ministry; chaired by Cabinet Secretary; members = Home Secretary + Secretary to President + 4-6 eminent persons). (3) Committee recommends to PM + PRESIDENT. (4) President APPROVES. (5) ANNOUNCED on REPUBLIC DAY EVE (25 Jan); presented at RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN Durbar Hall in March-April by PRESIDENT. ANNUAL NUMBERS: max ~120 Padma Awards (incl. Vibhushan + Bhushan + Shri) per year. Padma Vibhushan: 5-7 typically; Bhushan: 20-30; Shri: 80-100. No posthumous Padma for persons who died >3 years prior (SPECIAL cases can be exceptions). Cannot be refused publicly without renouncing — e.g., BAUL SINGER SUBODHCHANDRA NAYAK, PATRIOT PROF. C.N.R. RAO's son, SITARA DEVI (declined 2002 Padma Bhushan — felt she deserved Bharat Ratna or higher), historian ROMILA THAPAR (refused Padma Bhushan 1992, 2005). UNIQUE FEATURES: Padma awards are NOT TITLES (per Art 18) — cannot prefix names. No monetary benefit. BENEFITS: prestige + some ceremonial rights + state protocol. CASH prizes come only with some specific fields (e.g., Jnanpith — literature). MILITARY GALLANTRY AWARDS — separate hierarchy: (1) PARAM VIR CHAKRA (PVC) — highest wartime. (2) MAHA VIR CHAKRA (MVC). (3) VIR CHAKRA (VrC). PEACETIME: (1) ASHOK CHAKRA (AC) — highest peacetime. (2) KIRTI CHAKRA (KC). (3) SHAURYA CHAKRA (SC). FORCE-specific: (4) PARAM VISHISHT SEVA MEDAL (PVSM) — distinguished service. (5) AVSM (Ati Vishisht Seva Medal). (6) VSM (Vishisht Seva Medal). PRESIDENT'S POLICE MEDAL + Police Medal for Gallantry + Distinguished Service. SPORTS AWARDS: (1) MAJOR DHYAN CHAND KHEL RATNA (ex-Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) — highest sport award; renamed 2021. (2) ARJUNA AWARD. (3) DRONACHARYA AWARD (coaches). (4) DHYAN CHAND AWARD (lifetime contribution). LITERARY: (1) JNANPITH AWARD — highest Indian literary award (est. 1961 by Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain Bharatiya Jnanpith foundation); 1.1M + bronze Saraswati. (2) SAHITYA AKADEMI AWARD (annual, per language, 24 languages). FILM: DADASAHEB PHALKE AWARD (highest film, since 1969, for lifetime contribution — given at National Film Awards). (DPA): Devika Rani (1969 first), recent Waheeda Rehman (2023). NATIONAL FILM AWARDS — annual; established 1954.

questions.stem: The FIRST sportsperson to receive BHARAT RATNA (2014) was:
questions.explanation: SACHIN RAMESH TENDULKAR (b. 24 April 1973) — 'GOD OF CRICKET'; 'Little Master'; arguably CRICKET's GREATEST BATSMAN. FIRST SPORTSPERSON to receive BHARAT RATNA — announced 16 NOVEMBER 2013 (the very day he RETIRED from international cricket after his 200th Test at Wankhede). Medal received 4 February 2014 from President Pranab Mukherjee. At 40 years = YOUNGEST Bharat Ratna recipient ever. Prior minimum age for civilian honours was often higher. The rule was AMENDED 2011 to include sports (previously sports had separate awards — Khel Ratna). CRICKET RECORDS: (1) Most INTERNATIONAL runs ever — 34,357 (across 664 matches; Tests + ODIs + T20s). (2) ONLY player with 100 INTERNATIONAL CENTURIES (51 Tests + 49 ODIs). (3) Most TEST runs — 15,921 in 200 Tests (record held till Virat Kohli's overtaking likely future). (4) Most ODI runs — 18,426 in 463 ODIs. (5) ONLY cricketer to score DOUBLE CENTURY in ODI — 200* vs South Africa at Gwalior, 24 Feb 2010. (6) Debut at 16 YEARS (15 Nov 1989 at Karachi vs Pakistan — youngest Indian Test debutant at 16 yrs 205 days). (7) First batsman to 10,000 + 12,000 + 14,000 + 15,000 Test runs. (8) Played in 6 WORLD CUPS (1992, 1996, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011) — most by any cricketer. (9) WON 2011 WORLD CUP ('I have carried the nation for 21 years; today, the team carried me' — quote from teammates). FINAL Test match 14-16 Nov 2013 at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai. Emotional farewell speech. TEAM INDIA won 2011 ICC World Cup at same Wankhede. OTHER HONOURS: Arjuna Award 1994, Padma Shri 1999, Khel Ratna 1997-98, Padma Vibhushan 2008, BHARAT RATNA 2014. Inducted into ICC Hall of Fame 2019. Rajya Sabha MP (2012-18, NOMINATED). OTHER SPORTING BHARAT RATNA: None (Sachin remains the ONLY sportsperson with BR as of 2025). 'GOD OF CRICKET' nickname by Matthew Hayden; Sir Don Bradman called Sachin 'the closest modern batsman to himself' (invited to his 90th birthday 1998). CHARITABLE: Sachin Tendulkar Foundation; Apnalaya (slum children); Wanted Dead or Alive for educating poor children. FAMOUS QUOTES: 'Cricket is my first love'; 'Play with a straight bat'; 'Chase your dreams'. MAJOR DHYAN CHAND — 'HOCKEY WIZARD' (1905-79) — 3 Olympic gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936); scored 400+ international goals. Awarded PADMA BHUSHAN 1956 (before Khel Ratna existed). Demands to posthumously award him Bharat Ratna still ongoing — birthday 29 Aug = NATIONAL SPORTS DAY since 2012; Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna renamed MAJOR DHYAN CHAND KHEL RATNA in Aug 2021. OTHER ICONIC Indian sportspersons: Kapil Dev (1983 WC captain), Sunil Gavaskar (first to 10,000 Test runs), Mahendra Singh Dhoni (3 ICC trophies captain — T20 2007, ODI 2011, CT 2013), Virat Kohli (modern great), Abhinav Bindra (first individual Olympic gold 2008 shooting), Neeraj Chopra (javelin gold Tokyo 2020, Paris silver 2024), P.V. Sindhu (badminton, Rio 2016 silver, Tokyo 2020 bronze), P.T. Usha, Milkha Singh, Viswanathan Anand (5x world chess champion 2000-13), Mary Kom (6x world boxing champ), Sania Mirza, Saina Nehwal, Bhaichung Bhutia (football), Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Karnam Malleswari (weightlifting first woman Olympic medal 2000), Vijender Singh, Rani Rampal (hockey captain). 'God of Cricket'; 100 international centuries; announced 16 Nov 2013 (day of retirement); age 40 = YOUNGEST BR recipient.

questions.stem: India's HIGHEST literary award (one of world's largest) is:
questions.explanation: JNANPITH AWARD — India's HIGHEST literary honour; one of the largest + most prestigious in world. INSTITUTED 1961 by BHARATIYA JNANPITH foundation (established 1944 by the JAIN BUSINESS FAMILY — Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain + Rama Jain). Only for literature in languages listed in 8TH SCHEDULE of Constitution + ENGLISH (added 2013). Awarded ANNUALLY (though some gaps). CURRENT MONETARY VALUE: ₹11 LAKH CASH + Vagdevi (Saraswati) bronze idol + citation. PROCESS: nominated + selected by JNANPITH SELECTION BOARD (chaired in past by poets + scholars of stature — currently by Pratibha Ray). FIRST RECIPIENT: G. SHANKARA KURUP (1965) — for 'Odakkuzhal' (Malayalam, 1950). 2nd: Tarashankar Bandyopadhyay (1966, Bengali). Notable RECIPIENTS: (a) RAMDHARI SINGH 'DINKAR' (1972, Hindi 'Urvashi'). (b) UR ANANTHAMURTHY (1994, Kannada). (c) MAHASWETA DEVI (1996, Bengali). (d) GIRISH KARNAD (1998, Kannada). (e) GURDIAL SINGH (1999, Punjabi). (f) INDIRA GOSWAMI (2000, Assamese). (g) RAJENDRA SHAH (2001, Gujarati). (h) JAYAKANTHAN (2002, Tamil). (i) VINDA KARANDIKAR (2003, Marathi). (j) K. AYYAPPA PANIKER (2004, Malayalam). (k) KUNWAR NARAYAN (2005, Hindi). (l) RAVURI BHARADWAJA (2012, Telugu). (m) KEDARNATH SINGH (2013, Hindi). (n) BHALCHANDRA NEMADE (2014, Marathi). (o) RAGHUVEER CHAUDHARI (2015, Gujarati). (p) SHANKHA GHOSH (2016, Bengali). (q) KRISHNA SOBTI (2017, Hindi). (r) AMITAV GHOSH (2018 — first winner for ENGLISH). (s) AKKITHAM ACHUTHAN NAMBOOTHIRI (2019, Malayalam). (t) NILAMANI PHOOKAN (2021, Assamese). (u) DAMODAR MAUZO (2022, Konkani). (v) GULZAR + RAMBHADRACHARYA (2023 JOINT — Urdu + Sanskrit). NOTE: MAHADEVI VARMA was the FIRST WOMAN Jnanpith winner (1982, Hindi). KANNADA leads in Jnanpiths (8 winners), then HINDI (11), then BENGALI (6), MALAYALAM (6), URDU (5). NEVER won by TAMIL alone significantly (3 winners). LANGUAGES still awaiting Jnanpith: Sindhi, Kashmiri, Bodo, Santali, Maithili, Dogri, Manipuri, Nepali. SAHITYA AKADEMI AWARD — separate — annual literary prize given in each of 24 official languages + ENGLISH; est. 1954; ₹1 LAKH prize; very different from Jnanpith (which covers all languages + one person/year). Sahitya Akademi also has FELLOWSHIPS (supreme honor; higher than annual awards) — only ~21 Fellows at a time (for lifetime contribution). Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for young writers. BAL SAHITYA PURASKAR for children's lit. NOBEL PRIZE IN LITERATURE — Rabindranath Tagore (1913, 'Gitanjali') — India's ONLY Nobel in Literature. Nominees include R.K. Narayan + others, never won. established 1961 by Bharatiya Jnanpith foundation (Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain); ₹11 lakh cash + bronze Saraswati idol + citation.

questions.stem: INDIA's highest PEACETIME GALLANTRY AWARD is:
questions.explanation: ASHOK CHAKRA — India's HIGHEST PEACETIME MILITARY GALLANTRY AWARD. Equivalent in peacetime to PARAM VIR CHAKRA (wartime). INSTITUTED 4 January 1952 as 'Ashoka Chakra Class I'; renamed 'Ashok Chakra' 1967. AWARDED for 'most conspicuous bravery or some act of daring or pre-eminent valour or self-sacrifice' OTHERWISE than in FACE of the ENEMY (i.e., not wartime front-line). Covers counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency operations, internal security, rescue/disaster operations. DESIGN: circular gold medallion with Ashoka Chakra engraved; green ribbon with 2 orange vertical stripes. AWARD PROCESS: recommended by unit commander → MHA's military awards committee → President approves. Often POSTHUMOUS. AWARDED: ~96 times till 2024; mostly POSTHUMOUS. NOTABLE RECIPIENTS: (1) NAIK NARBAHADUR THAPA (1952) — FIRST recipient; for rescuing drowning colleagues. (2) MAJOR D. SREERAM KUMAR (1965). (3) LT Col. N.J. NAIR (1988, Sri Lanka IPKF). (4) Captain MAHENDRA NATH MULLA (1971 — posthumous; drowned with INS Khukri rather than abandon crew). (5) MAJOR SANDEEP UNNIKRISHNAN (2008, NSG commando; died combating 26/11 Mumbai attack; posthumous; 'Ullasa + fearless' commander). (6) MAJOR MOHIT SHARMA (2009 posthumous, Kashmir CT ops). (7) HAVILDAR BACHITTAR SINGH (1952). (8) HAVILDAR HANGPAN DADA (2016 posthumous, Kashmir CT). (9) MAJOR PADMAPANI ACHARYA (earlier MVC; part of Kargil posthumous). (10) COLONEL SANTOSH BABU (2020 posthumous, GALWAN VALLEY clash 15-16 June 2020, commanded 16 Bihar; India's first combat death with China since 1975). (11) MAJOR BHOOPATI (EARLIER). (12) Flt Lt Shipra Majumdar (first woman AC?). (13) Various NSG + SPG + CRPF commandos. (14) LANCE HAV MOHAN NATH GOSWAMI (2016 posthumous). LATEST: Havildar (Sub retd.) Sanjay Kumar + Chief Constable Swapandeep Bannerjee (2024). ASHOK CHAKRA is followed by: (2) KIRTI CHAKRA (2nd highest peacetime). (3) SHAURYA CHAKRA (3rd highest peacetime). All 3 awarded for gallantry in non-war situations — counter-terrorism, insurgency, rescue. WARTIME gallantry (in face of enemy): (1) PARAM VIR CHAKRA (PVC, highest) — 21 awardees. (2) MAHA VIR CHAKRA (MVC). (3) VIR CHAKRA (VrC). INSTITUTED 26 Jan 1950; retrospective to 15 Aug 1947 (for Kashmir War). OTHER gallantry/service awards: Sena Medal (Army), Nao Sena Medal (Navy), Vayu Sena Medal (Air Force), Yudh Seva Medal, Sarvottam Yudh Seva, Uttam Yudh Seva. DISTINGUISHED SERVICE: Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM), Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM), Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM). POLICE: President's Police Medal (PPM), Police Medal for Gallantry (PMG), Police Medal for Distinguished Service (PMD). PRESIDENT'S COLOURS — highest unit award; conferred on select regiments + squadrons. STATE POLICE specific awards. FIRE SERVICE / HOME GUARDS / CIVIL DEFENCE medals. BSF + CRPF + ITBP + CISF + Assam Rifles each have their own gallantry medals. equivalent to Param Vir Chakra (wartime); awarded for valour in non-war operations (counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency, peace).

questions.stem: The DADASAHEB PHALKE AWARD, India's highest FILM honour, was instituted in 1969. It is named after:
questions.explanation: DADASAHEB PHALKE AWARD — India's highest FILM honour; presented annually at the NATIONAL FILM AWARDS ceremony by PRESIDENT. Instituted 1969 by Government of India to commemorate DHUNDIRAJ GOVIND PHALKE's contribution to Indian Cinema. AWARDED for 'outstanding contribution to the growth + development of Indian cinema' — LIFETIME achievement basis. DADASAHEB PHALKE (30 Apr 1870 – 16 Feb 1944) — 'FATHER OF INDIAN CINEMA' / 'PITAMAHA of Indian cinema'. Born Maharashtra (Trimbak, Nashik). Raised in Brahmin family; cultural background (sculpture, photography). Attended J.J. School of Art Mumbai; trained in photography + LITHOGRAPHY. SET UP printing press; various ventures. Deeply moved by 'LIFE OF CHRIST' film (1910 Christmas Bombay screening); decided to make first Indian feature. Sold house + borrowed money; bought camera + film equipment from Britain. MADE 'RAJA HARISHCHANDRA' (1913) — INDIA's FIRST FULL-LENGTH FEATURE FILM (silent, 40 minutes). Shot on black + white; cast of all-MALE actors (including for female roles — women actors not yet accepted in mainstream; earlier cinema acts could only use men for female roles per convention). Released 3 May 1913 at Coronation Cinematograph Bombay (first commercial screening 21 April 1913 at Olympia Theatre; public 3 May). First 'swadeshi' film. Launched HINDUSTAN FILM COMPANY at Nashik — produced 27 films in next 15 years (all silent era). Notable: Mohini Bhasmasur (1913), Satyavan Savitri, Lanka Dahan (1917 — massive hit), Shri Krishna Janma, Kaliya Mardan (1919). Phalke went BANKRUPT; died poverty 1944. AWARD RECIPIENTS (select, cash ₹10 lakh + Swarna Kamal gold lotus medallion + shawl): (1) DEVIKA RANI (1969) — FIRST recipient; 'First Lady of Indian Cinema'. (2) Birendranath Sircar (1970). (3) PRITHVIRAJ KAPOOR posthumous (1971). (4) Pankaj Mullick (1972). (5) Sulochana Devi (1973). (6) B.N. Reddi (1974). (7) Dhiren Ganguly (1975). (8) K. Subrahmanyam (1980). (9) DIRECTOR/FILMMAKERS: Satyajit Ray (1984), V. Shantaram (1985), Hrishikesh Mukherjee (1999), B.R. Chopra (2001), Adoor Gopalakrishnan (2004), MRINAL SEN (2005), Tapan Sinha (2006), K. Balachander (2010), Soumitra Chatterjee (2012), RAMOJI RAO (2009). (10) ACTORS: ASHOK KUMAR (1988), Raj Kapoor (1987), DILIP KUMAR (1994), DEV ANAND (2002), SHYAM BENEGAL (2019), K. Viswanath (2016), SHATRUGHAN SINHA (2013), AMITABH BACHCHAN (2018). (11) MUSIC: NAUSHAD (1982), LATA MANGESHKAR (1989), ASHA BHOSLE (2000), A.R. RAHMAN — never Phalke (got Oscar + Bharat Ratna not Phalke). (12) COMPOSERS: SHANKAR-JAIKISHAN, MANNA DEY, MAHENDRA KAPOOR. (13) RECENT: REKHA (2023 at 2021 Ceremony), WAHEEDA REHMAN (2023 at 2023 ceremony — October), MITHUN CHAKRABORTY (2024, 70th NFA announced Aug 2024). NATIONAL FILM AWARDS est. 1954; Swarna + Rajat Kamals. FIRST PHALKE WINNER: DEVIKA RANI (1908-94) — actress-producer; founded Bombay Talkies; wife of Himanshu Rai + later S. Svetoslav Roerich. 'FATHER OF INDIAN CINEMA'; made India's first full-length feature 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913, silent).

questions.stem: India's NOBEL PRIZE laureates include (only Indian citizens):

options.option_text: RABINDRANATH TAGORE (Lit 1913), C.V. RAMAN (Phy 1930), MOTHER TERESA (Peace 1979), AMARTYA SEN (Eco 1998), KAILASH SATYARTHI

questions.explanation: NOBEL LAUREATES of INDIAN ORIGIN — INDIAN CITIZENS AT TIME OF AWARD (5): (1) RABINDRANATH TAGORE (1861-1941) — LITERATURE 1913 — for 'GITANJALI' ('Song Offerings'); FIRST non-European Nobel in Literature; FIRST Asian Nobel in any field. Translated his Bengali poems into English himself + W.B. Yeats. Composed national anthems of India (Jana Gana Mana) + Bangladesh (Amar Sonar Bangla). Founded Santiniketan/Visva-Bharati. Renounced knighthood 1919 after Jallianwala. (2) Sir C.V. RAMAN (1888-1970) — PHYSICS 1930 — for DISCOVERY of RAMAN EFFECT (inelastic scattering of light); discovered 28 Feb 1928; Indian scientist in Calcutta at IACS. Later founded Raman Research Institute Bengaluru. 28 Feb = National Science Day. FIRST Asian Nobel in science. (3) MOTHER TERESA (1910-97) — PEACE 1979 — for humanitarian work with Missionaries of Charity (founded 1950 in Calcutta); Indian citizen since 1951 (naturalised); Albanian-born. Received Bharat Ratna 1980. Canonised as SAINT TERESA OF CALCUTTA 2016 by Pope Francis. (4) AMARTYA SEN (b. 1933) — ECONOMICS (formal: Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel) 1998 — for WELFARE ECONOMICS, capability approach, social choice theory, poverty measurement (Sen index), gender studies, human development. Bengali; Cambridge + Harvard professor. 'MOTHER OF CAPABILITY APPROACH'. Books: 'Poverty + Famines', 'Development as Freedom', 'The Idea of Justice', 'The Argumentative Indian'. Indian citizen. (5) KAILASH SATYARTHI (b. 1954) — PEACE 2014 (SHARED with Malala Yousafzai of Pakistan) — for struggle against child labour + for child rights; founded BBA (Bachpan Bachao Andolan) 1980; rescued 100,000+ children from bonded labour / trafficking; Global March Against Child Labour. INDIAN-ORIGIN LAUREATES with FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP at time of award: (a) HAR GOBIND KHORANA (1922-2011) — Medicine 1968 (with Nirenberg + Holley) — interpretation of genetic code + protein synthesis; Indian-American (born Punjab, Wisconsin-MIT later). (b) SUBRAHMANYAN CHANDRASEKHAR (1910-95) — Physics 1983 — Chandrasekhar limit (stellar evolution); Indian-American (MI-Bombay-Chicago). NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory named after him. Nephew of CV Raman. (c) V.S. NAIPAUL (1932-2018) — Literature 2001 — Trinidadian-born British; Indian origin. Novels on post-colonial identity. (d) VENKATRAMAN RAMAKRISHNAN (b. 1952) — Chemistry 2009 — ribosome structure; Indian-born American (Chidambaram TN → Ohio → Cambridge UK). Was president of Royal Society 2015-20. (e) ABHIJIT BANERJEE (b. 1961) — Economics 2019 (with Esther Duflo + Michael Kremer) — experimental approach to alleviating global poverty; Randomised Control Trials (RCTs); MIT prof, US citizen, Indian-origin, wife Duflo is co-awardee (2nd woman + youngest Eco Nobel). MANY OTHER Indian origin contributions: (a) PRANAB BARDHAN, JAGDISH BHAGWATI, GITA GOPINATH (IMF), RAGHURAM RAJAN — major economists, not Nobel (yet). (b) GOPI HINDURAO, C.N.R. RAO (world-class chemist, Bharat Ratna 2014) — world contributions. India UNDER-REPRESENTED in Nobels given its population + scientific potential — active discussion in policy + science circles. 5 native-born Nobel laureates as Indian citizens.

questions.stem: The RAMON MAGSAYSAY AWARD, often called 'ASIA's NOBEL PRIZE', is awarded by:
questions.explanation: RAMON MAGSAYSAY AWARD — 'Asia's NOBEL PRIZE'. ESTABLISHED April 1957 by RAMON MAGSAYSAY AWARD FOUNDATION (Manila) in memory of late Philippine President RAMON MAGSAYSAY (1907-1957, killed in plane crash at age 49; known as 'Champion of the Masses', anti-Huk insurgency leader, simple + populist; 3rd President of Philippines 1953-57). Foundation funded by ROCKEFELLER BROTHERS FUND (New York). FIRST awards 1958. AWARDED ANNUALLY on 31 AUGUST (Ramon Magsaysay's birth anniversary) by Philippine President. 6 CATEGORIES originally + later additions: (1) Government Service; (2) Public Service; (3) Community Leadership; (4) Journalism, Literature + Creative Communication Arts; (5) Peace + International Understanding; (6) Emergent Leadership (added 2000, for under-40). Categories consolidated in 2008 to broader 'Emergent Leadership' + general award. MONEY PRIZE: ~US $50,000 per awardee. INDIAN RECIPIENTS (significant tally — among most globally): ~60 Indians till 2024 — MOST of any country besides Philippines. SELECT INDIAN recipients: (1) ACHARYA VINOBA BHAVE (1958 — FIRST Indian recipient; Bhoodan Movement). (2) C.D. DESHMUKH (1959, first RBI Indian Gov). (3) AMITABHA CHAUDHURI (1961, journalism). (4) MOTHER TERESA (1962). (5) WELTHY FISHER (1964, literacy). (6) S. CHANDRASEKHAR (1966, demographer). (7) M.S. SUBBULAKSHMI (1974, FIRST musician; Carnatic vocal). (8) V. KURIEN (1974, White Revolution Operation Flood). (9) MAHASWETA DEVI (1997, activist-writer). (10) T.N. SESHAN (1996, Chief Election Commissioner who transformed ECI). (11) JAMES MICHAEL LYNGDOH (2003, CEC during Gujarat elections). (12) ARUN SHOURIE (1982, journalism). (13) B.G. VERGHESE (1975, journalism). (14) M.S. SWAMINATHAN (1971, Green Revolution; also got WORLD FOOD PRIZE 1987 + Bharat Ratna 2024). (15) RAJENDRA SINGH (2001, 'Water Man of India'; Tarun Bharat Sangh reviving Rajasthan water). (16) ARVIND KEJRIWAL (2006, RTI + Parivartan; now Delhi CM AAP). (17) RAVISH KUMAR (2019, journalism, NDTV Hindi). (18) BEZWADA WILSON (2016, Safai Karamchari Andolan — sanitation worker rights). (19) T.M. KRISHNA (2016, Carnatic musician + social commentary). (20) BHARAT VATWANI (2018, Shraddha Rehabilitation Foundation — mental illness homeless). (21) SONAM WANGCHUK (2018, educationist-innovator Ladakh, inspiration for 3 Idiots Rancho; ice stupa + cheap solar). (22) GUNEETA SINGH BHALLA (2017?). (23) PALAGUMMI SAINATH (2007, rural journalism — People's Archive of Rural India). Also ELA BHATT (1977, SEWA), KIRAN BEDI (1994, first woman IPS; prison reform), KAILASH SATYARTHI (1994 — before his Nobel 2014). OTHER PRESTIGIOUS international prizes won by INDIANS: WORLD FOOD PRIZE (M.S. Swaminathan 1987, Dr. Verghese Kurien never (despite deserving), Norman Borlaug types); BORLAUG AWARD; UN prizes; WORLD TEACHER PRIZE (Ranjitsinh Disale 2020, Maharashtra); MILLION DOLLAR TEACHER PRIZE; TAGORE PEACE PRIZE; TYLER PRIZE; GAIRDNER (Canada). RAMON MAGSAYSAY remains most prestigious Asian award. Foundation now based in Philippines; reduced funding; occasional controversy about recipients. est. 1957 in honour of late Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay; 6 categories; won by many eminent Indians.

questions.stem: Rule for BHARAT RATNA — maximum number of recipients per year (conventionally):
questions.explanation: BHARAT RATNA — PER-YEAR LIMIT: 3 per year (conventionally, per original notification 1954). Sometimes this convention is relaxed: (a) 2024 had 5 AWARDEES (post-facto for various years' delayed decisions). 4 on 9 Feb 2024 + 1 more (MS Swaminathan + Narasimha Rao + Charan Singh + Karpoori Thakur on 23 Jan 2024 had been announced). Advani announced 3 February. (b) 1999 had 4 awardees (JRD Tata, Satyajit Ray, M. Vishvesvaraya were earlier — this was unusual). TOTAL RECIPIENTS till 2024: 53 persons. 2024 alone: FIVE recipients announced. YEARS WITH NO BHARAT RATNA — several years (e.g., 1956, 1959, 1960, 1964, 1967-70, 1972-74, 1976-79, 1981-82, 1984-86, 1989, 1993, 1996, 2000-2007 except 2001, 2009, 2010-13, 2017, 2020-22). Awards clustered in certain years. POSTHUMOUS — recently almost all have been posthumous — 9 of last 12 (2015-2024). OLDEST AT RECEIVING: D. DEVARAJ URS (1976)? MS SUBBULAKSHMI was 82; PRANAB MUKHERJEE was 83. YOUNGEST AT RECEIVING: Sachin Tendulkar at 40 (2014); Indira Gandhi at 54 (1971); Rajiv Gandhi at 47 (1991 posthumous). INDIAN PRESIDENTS who received Bharat Ratna (in chronological order): RAJENDRA PRASAD (1962, post-presidency 1950-62), S. RADHAKRISHNAN (1954, pre- + during VP-days), Dr ZAKIR HUSSAIN (1963, before becoming President 1967-69), V.V. GIRI (1975, post), INDIRA GANDHI (1971, during PM), A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM (1997, before becoming Pres 2002-07), PRANAB MUKHERJEE (2019, post-presidency 2012-17). Future PM or PRES ASPIRANTS wait. PM/CM RECIPIENTS: Nehru (1955, while PM), Indira Gandhi (1971 while PM), MGR (1988, TN CM), Rajiv Gandhi (1991 posthumous), Atal Bihari Vajpayee (2015), Narasimha Rao (2024 posthumous), Charan Singh (2024 posthumous), Karpoori Thakur (2024 posthumous). ALL PMs/PRES received if still alive post-retirement? NO — Manmohan Singh, Deve Gowda, Gujral, Chandra Shekhar, V.P. Singh etc. did not. Controversial. CONTROVERSIES / DEMANDS: (1) Jawaharlal Nehru gave himself Bharat Ratna 1955 (as PM recommending to President; widely criticised; many feel he should have waited or it should be given posthumously). Indira similarly 1971. Both controversies. (2) CHAUDHARY DEVI LAL refused Bharat Ratna. SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE was OFFERED posthumous 1992 Bharat Ratna; family REFUSED unless proof of his death (still maintaining doubts); Government WITHDREW the offer. (3) DEMANDS for posthumous Bharat Ratna to: Major Dhyan Chand (hockey), Ram Manohar Lohia, Kanshi Ram, Mulayam, E. Sreedharan, Maharshi Dayanand, Subrahmanya Bharathi (declined), Rajiv Gandhi (got), Veer Savarkar (demand + opposition), Guru Gobind Singh etc. (4) 2024's FIVE awardees seen as POLITICAL gesture preceding Lok Sabha elections by critics (Advani BJP, Charan Singh Jats, Karpoori Thakur OBCs, Rao Telangana, Swaminathan farmers). BHARAT RATNA rules: (a) recommendation by PM to Pres. (b) Cannot be used as title (Art 18). (c) No cash. (d) Certificate + Medal. (e) Posthumous OK. (f) 3 max convention. ORDER of PRECEDENCE: rank 7a (high official protocol). Rao, Charan Singh, Swaminathan, Advani, Karpoori Thakur. many years have NONE or 1-2 awardees; 2024 was unusual with 5 recipients.
